slides.title: SocietyBench: Forecasting Counterfactual Social-World Evolution
slides.tldr: BENCHMARK FOR FORECASTING SOCIAL-WORLD EVOLUTION
slides.highlight: SocietyBench evaluates the ability of LLM agents to forecast social event unfoldings using counterfactual timelines, supporting MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and impact analysis.

card.one_liner: SocietyBench evaluates LLM forecasting of social events using anonymized, counterfactual timelines to prevent pre-training memory recall.
card.key_idea: Real social events are transformed into counterfactual worlds via entity substitution and date shifting, then scored on probability calibration and temporal accuracy.
card.evaluation: Six frontier LLMs, three agent frameworks, and two heuristics were tested on five heterogeneous events; GPT-5.5 performed best (75.0/100).
card.limitation: High per-event score variance (up to 21.4 points) makes single-event evaluations unreliable for comparing model performance.

slides.title: Designing Social Robots for Inclusive Child Wellbeing Assessment: Insights from Communities Supporting Developmental Language Disorder and Forced Migration
slides.tldr: INCLUSIVE ROBOT-MEDIATED WELLBEING ASSESSMENT
slides.highlight: This research provides design recommendations for using social robots to assess the wellbeing of children with communication barriers, supporting the RwB focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: Design guidelines for inclusive social robot-mediated wellbeing assessments for children with communication barriers and forced migration backgrounds.
card.key_idea: Used interdisciplinary design probes and focus groups with parents and professionals to identify ethical and inclusive requirements for robot-led wellbeing assessments.
card.evaluation: Thematic analysis of focus group discussions with 14 stakeholders (parents and professionals) across two specific vulnerable child populations.
card.limitation: The study relies on stakeholder perspectives (parents/professionals) rather than direct interaction data from the children themselves.

slides.title: Humanoid Companion Robot Market Projected to Reach US$1.1bn by 2030
slides.tldr: GROWTH IN HUMANOID COMPANION ROBOT MARKET
slides.highlight: The increasing demand for caregiving and emotional support is driving market growth for humanoid companion robots. This trend aligns with RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

slides.title: No One Wins in Nuclear War: A Social Simulation of Military Decision-making
slides.tldr: SOCIAL SIMULATION OF HIGH-STAKES MILITARY DECISION-MAKING
slides.highlight: Introduces WOPR, a social-simulation environment with a verifiable rules engine and collective command-and-control systems, relevant to MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and agent models.

card.one_liner: WOPR is a social-simulation environment for studying high-stakes organizational decision-making via a verifiable rules engine.
card.key_idea: A deterministic, replay-validated engine using a decision-point contract, a four-rung communication 'press ladder', and four distinct command-and-control archetypes for collective faction decision-making.
card.evaluation: Verified via a 240-game sweep ensuring seeded outcomes are preserved; instantiated using the card game Nuclear War with a rule conformance matrix.
card.limitation: Early-stage tool; lacks controlled studies, large-scale press mode evaluation, and automated enforcement of agent commitments.

slides.title: TIDES: A Longitudinal Bilingual Dataset for Modeling Multi-Party Social Dynamics
slides.tldr: LONGITUDINAL DATASET FOR MULTI-PARTY SOCIAL DYNAMICS
slides.highlight: TIDES provides a longitudinal dataset of real-world team interactions with annotations on emergent roles and interaction types, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and group norms.

card.one_liner: TIDES is a longitudinal bilingual dataset of university project teams used to model multi-party social dynamics.
card.key_idea: A dataset of 75,971 utterances with socio-structural annotations (interaction types, emergent roles, development stages) to improve LLM next-speaker prediction and structural understanding in group conversations.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via next-speaker/intention prediction and AMI Corpus transfer. Fine-tuning improved speaker prediction by 13.8pp over bigram baseline; human evaluation used Prolific judges.
card.limitation: Improved structural prediction does not necessarily translate to more natural or coherent utterance generation, as vanilla models were preferred by humans.

slides.title: Hybrid Attention Estimation Pipeline for Adaptive HRI Using an Expressive Robotic Head
slides.tldr: HYBRID ATTENTION ESTIMATION FOR ADAPTIVE HRI
slides.highlight: This work proposes a pipeline combining geometric and semantic perception to regulate adaptive interaction behaviors in an expressive robotic head, contributing to the development of embodied social robots for RwB.

card.one_liner: A hybrid attention-estimation pipeline for an expressive robotic head to enable adaptive human-robot interaction.
card.key_idea: Combines a fast geometric layer (MediaPipe head-pose) for real-time state regulation with a VLM-based semantic layer (LLaVA-Phi3) for contextual attention labeling via a finite state machine.
card.evaluation: Tested with 10 participants over 40 trials. Results showed reliable interaction starts and consistent adaptive pause/resume behaviors in distraction scenarios.
card.limitation: Controlled experimental setup, small participant sample, and lack of manual frame-level ground truth for attention labels.

slides.title: Staged Multi-Agent Training (SMAT) for Hip Exoskeletons: Metabolic and Biomechanical Validation of a Simulation-Trained Co-Adaptive Controller
slides.tldr: SIMULATION-TRAINED CO-ADAPTIVE EXOSKELETON CONTROL
slides.highlight: This work introduces Staged Multi-Agent Training (SMAT) to address the non-stationary learning problem of human-device co-adaptation, aligning with MOSAIC's focus on coadaptive loops and skill acquisition.

card.one_liner: A simulation-trained co-adaptive controller for hip exoskeletons significantly reduces metabolic walking cost in real users.
card.key_idea: Staged Multi-Agent Training (SMAT) uses a four-stage curriculum to sequentially train a musculoskeletal human actor and an exoskeleton actor, addressing non-stationary co-adaptation through isolated learning phases.
card.evaluation: Tested on eight healthy adults using indirect calorimetry and biomechanical analysis; active assistance reduced net metabolic rate by 19.7% relative to the passive device.
card.limitation: Not clearly stated.

slides.title: Is Inter-Seed Cross-Play Enough? Evaluating the Robustness of Zero-Shot Coordination Algorithms to Implementation Details
slides.tldr: ROBUSTNESS EVALUATION OF ZERO-SHOT COORDINATION
slides.highlight: This research evaluates the robustness of zero-shot coordination algorithms to implementation details, which is relevant to ADAM-CHAT's goal of creating AI teammates that can coordinate with partners they have not encountered before.

card.one_liner: Inter-seed cross-play is a reliable proxy for evaluating zero-shot coordination robustness across different implementations.
card.key_idea: Introduces cross-implementation cross-play (XIXP), varying PPO implementation details (e.g., learning rate, weight initialization) to test if ZSC algorithms remain robust beyond random seed variation.
card.evaluation: Evaluated Other-Play using IPPO in the Yokai environment; compared within-implementation vs. cross-implementation scores across 11 competent implementations. Results show no significant performance gap.
card.limitation: Analysis is restricted to a single environment (Yokai), one base algorithm (IPPO), and one ZSC algorithm (Other-Play).

slides.title: Dobot Launches Full-Scenario Embodied Humanoid Robot
slides.tldr: NEW MULTI-FUNCTIONAL EMBODIED HUMANOID ROBOT
slides.highlight: Dobot has introduced a multi-functional embodied humanoid robot designed for daily and professional needs, providing a reference for RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: When AI Joins the Team! A Model of How AI Adoption Relates To Social Patterns in Software Engineering Teams
slides.tldr: AI ADOPTION AND TEAM SOCIAL DYNAMICS
slides.highlight: This research examines how AI adoption influences social patterns and communication quality in software teams, contributing to HyECHO's focus on the social perception of hybrid human-AI team states.

card.one_liner: AI adoption reduces community smells via different mechanisms depending on whether the work involves specialization or coordination.
card.key_idea: Using PLS-SEM grounded in Transactive Memory Systems theory, the study models how AI adoption influences social anti-patterns through Human-AI and Human-Human interaction dimensions.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via survey data from 152 software professionals, expert validation, and Exploratory Factor Analysis; results are empirically validated through PLS-SEM.
card.limitation: The study relies on developers' perceptions of community smells rather than objective technical metrics or longitudinal data.

slides.title: The Calibration Floor: Format Repair Can Masquerade as Self-Correction at Small-to-Mid Scale
slides.tldr: FORMAT REPAIR MASKING SELF-CORRECTION
slides.highlight: This research demonstrates that perceived self-correction in language models often results from format repair rather than reasoning changes, which is critical for developing the self-monitoring and self-correction capabilities of ADAM-CHAT.

card.one_liner: Apparent LLM self-correction gains are often just format repairs masquerading as reasoning improvements.
card.key_idea: Decomposes accuracy shifts into a 'content margin' (both answers parseable) and 'format margins' (parseability changes), using grammar-constrained decoding to causally isolate reasoning effects.
card.evaluation: Tested on Qwen3.5 (0.8B-9B), Gemma-4-12B, and frontier models across 29 cells (GSM8K, MMLU, etc.) using a calibration-floor criterion and causal controls.
card.limitation: Frontier model testing was lower-powered due to API rate limits and missing logprobs; MATH grader uses string normalization rather than symbolic equivalence.

slides.title: Chat Debugging: An Exploratory Study of Human-AI Collaboration to Debug Analog Circuits
slides.tldr: HUMAN-AI COLLABORATIVE ANALOG CIRCUIT DEBUGGING
slides.highlight: This study explores human-AI collaboration for debugging analog circuits, identifying gaps in LLM image-based reasoning and student skill levels relevant to the coadaptive loop of MOSAIC.

card.one_liner: Exploratory study on using off-the-shelf LLMs to help undergraduates debug analog circuits on breadboards/PCBs.
card.key_idea: Students used unstructured conversations and images with LLMs to generate debugging hypotheses, leveraging AI's domain knowledge to overcome novice experience gaps.
card.evaluation: Thematic analysis of 17 voluntary student chat logs and exam answer sheets from a one-year pilot study at OSU.
card.limitation: Small, self-selected sample size and LLM failures in 3D spatial reasoning for image-based circuit analysis.

slides.title: Deep Learning for Real-Time Sound Order Recognition in Human-Robot Interaction
slides.tldr: REAL-TIME SOUND ORDER RECOGNITION
slides.highlight: This research introduces a deep learning framework for recognizing the temporal order of overlapping sounds, which is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A deep learning framework for real-time recognition of the temporal order of overlapping non-verbal sounds.
card.key_idea: A multi-branch CNN processing Mel spectrograms, MFCCs, and STFT features, utilizing an attention-based fusion mechanism to identify sound sequences.
card.evaluation: Tested on synthetic overlaps (same/varied amplitude, unseen sounds); achieved 99% accuracy for balanced overlaps and 74% for unseen data.
card.limitation: Experiments relied on carefully controlled synthetic overlaps, raising concerns regarding ecological validity in real-room environments.

slides.title: Using Theory of Mind to Arbitrate between Social and Non-social Learning
slides.tldr: THEORY OF MIND FOR SOCIAL LEARNING ARBITRATION
slides.highlight: This research proposes a Rational Mentalizing model that uses Theory of Mind to balance social and non-social learning, aligning with ADAM-CHAT's focus on inferring partner intent via Theory of Mind.

card.one_liner: A model using Theory of Mind to decide when to observe others versus exploring independently.
card.key_idea: The Rational Mentalizing model uses Bayesian Theory of Mind to estimate the utility of social learning by simulating other agents' goals and beliefs against non-social costs.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via four grid-game experiments; the model achieved high agreement with human observation counts (pooled CCC = 0.89), outperforming three ablation baselines.
card.limitation: The model systematically underpredicts the absolute amount of observation and movement humans perform, potentially missing curiosity-driven or hedging behaviors.

slides.title: GradCuit: Credit-Assigned Gradient Flow Enables Robust and Interpretable Test-Time Latent Reasoning
slides.tldr: ROBUST TEST-TIME LATENT REASONING VIA GRADIENT FLOW
slides.highlight: GradCuit enables LLMs to adapt their reasoning process at test time by optimizing internal latent states based on outcome feedback, supporting ADAM-CHAT's goal of agents that adapt beyond in-context learning.

card.one_liner: GradCuit enables robust test-time latent reasoning by optimizing internal hidden states via direct gradient flow.
card.key_idea: Inserts optimizable latent states at intermediate Transformer layers, using self-attention as a differentiable circuit to assign reward-weighted gradients from generated tokens directly to latents.
card.evaluation: Tested on GPQA-Diamond, GSM8K, and MATH-500 across five backbones; outperformed CoT and LatentSeek with an average accuracy of 64.5%.
card.limitation: Optimal performance depends on the selected layer depth, with the most effective space typically being early-to-middle layers.

slides.title: Neuro-Symbolic Participation Governance for Verifiable AI Agents in Open Digital Twin Ecosystems
slides.tldr: NEURO-SYMBOLIC GOVERNANCE FOR VERIFIABLE AI AGENTS
slides.highlight: This work proposes a neuro-symbolic framework to bridge neural reasoning with deterministic governance for verifiable AI agents, supporting the MIMIC goal of simulating harmonious human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: A decentralized governance framework using neuro-symbolic profiles and blockchain to verify AI agent capabilities and compliance.
card.key_idea: Binds LLM agents to symbolic domain ontologies via Verifiable Credentials, using blockchain smart contracts for identity verification, dynamic role binding, and immutable interaction logging.
card.evaluation: Tested with 42 cases (security, policy, scalability) using a healthcare prototype; achieved 100% attack detection and O(1) verification complexity.
card.limitation: Focuses on admission governance and provenance; does not verify the actual quality or correctness of the agent's clinical recommendations.

slides.title: TacPrint: A Wearable Fingertip Tactile Sensor for Human-to-Robot Contact Reproduction
slides.tldr: WEARABLE FINGERTIP TACTILE SENSOR FOR SKILL TRANSFER
slides.highlight: TacPrint enables fine-grained capture of fingertip interactions to improve human-to-robot skill transfer in contact-rich tasks, supporting the MOSAIC goal of estimating procedural and tacit skills via force-based sensing.

card.one_liner: TacPrint is a low-cost wearable fingertip sensor enabling high-fidelity human-to-robot contact reproduction for manipulation tasks.
card.key_idea: A 24-channel capacitive sensor with silicone protrusions uses an LSTM-based real-to-sim-to-real pipeline to estimate dense 35×26 contact-depth maps from sparse tactile signals.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via controlled indentations, human-to-robot replay (grasping/wiping), and closed-loop grasping. Success rates improved from 0% to ~91% in replay tasks.
card.limitation: Sparse 24-channel input limits detailed shape reconstruction and may retain training indenter characteristics; pixel-level deformation was not fully validated.

slides.title: Cross-Task Dissociation in Frontier Vision-Language Model Theory of Mind
slides.tldr: VLMS SHOW INCONSISTENT THEORY-OF-MIND PROFILES ACROSS TASKS
slides.highlight: This research evaluates how frontier vision-language models perform on perspective-taking and intention attribution, showing a lack of a coherent Theory-of-Mind profile. This is relevant to ADAM-CHAT's goal of developing agents that can infer partners' intent via theory of mind.

card.one_liner: Frontier VLMs show fragmented Theory-of-Mind profiles, failing to align with a single human reference group across tasks.
card.key_idea: Evaluated nine VLMs on a paired suite: the Keysar Director Task (visual perspective-taking) and Frith-Happé animated triangles (intention attribution) to detect cross-task dissociation.
card.evaluation: Nine frontier VLMs tested across three trials per item; results compared to TD-adult and HF-ASD-adult reference profiles using distance metrics and rank association.
card.limitation: Results are panel-level descriptive, not diagnostic; animated-triangles scoring relies on LLM-as-rater, introducing a measurement noise floor compared to human raters.

slides.title: Evaluating Theory of Mind in Reasoning Models: Robustness over Reasoning
slides.tldr: ROBUSTNESS OF REASONING MODELS IN THEORY OF MIND TASKS
slides.highlight: This research examines how reasoning-oriented LLMs demonstrate increased robustness to prompt variations in Theory of Mind tasks, which is relevant to ADAM-CHAT's focus on inferring partner intent via theory of mind.

card.one_liner: Reasoning models improve Theory of Mind performance primarily through increased robustness rather than new cognitive abilities.
card.key_idea: The authors compare reasoning-oriented LLMs against non-reasoning counterparts using psychological tests and prompt perturbations to analyze stability in reaching correct answers under task variation.
card.evaluation: Evaluated using Sally-Anne, Strange Stories, and Imposing Memory tests, plus prompt modifications. Results show high accuracy and increased stability across reasoning models.
card.limitation: Behavioral analysis lacks causal identification of RLVR training effects; some tasks may rely on spurious correlations or meta-knowledge.

slides.authors: Ian B. de Haan et al.

slides.title: Human Centric Embodied Intelligence for Soft Wearable Robotics
slides.tldr: HUMAN-CENTRIC EMBODIED INTELLIGENCE FOR SOFT WEARABLES
slides.highlight: This review proposes the Perception-Cognition-Actuation-Augmentation framework to integrate sensing and adaptive cognition into wearable robots. It is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A review proposing the HCEI framework to shift soft wearable robotics from actuator-first to human-centric design.
card.key_idea: The Perception-Cognition-Actuation-Augmentation (PCAA) framework integrates morphology, multimodal sensing, and adaptive cognition to create intelligence through the coupled human-robot system.
card.evaluation: Not clearly stated; this is a conceptual review synthesizing advances across materials, AI, and clinical translation.
card.limitation: Not clearly stated.

slides.title: Accelerating Human-Aware Robot Trajectory Generation via Diffusion and Consistency Distillation
slides.tldr: FAST HUMAN-AWARE TRAJECTORY GENERATION
slides.highlight: This research introduces a framework using diffusion and consistency distillation to generate smooth, collision-aware robot trajectories for human-robot interaction. It is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: Accelerates human-aware robot trajectory generation using consistency distillation and jerk-regularized diffusion models.
card.key_idea: A conditional diffusion model trained on RRT/RRT* data, refined via constraint-guided sampling and consistency distillation for fast inference, with joint-weighted jerk regularization for smoothness.
card.evaluation: Simulated 6-DoF UR5 robot across 500 test scenes. Metrics included success rate, inference time, and jerk. Results show 98% faster inference than diffusion.
card.limitation: Evaluation was conducted exclusively in simulation; real-world robot performance and physical hardware constraints were not tested.

slides.title: RF-HOI: Recognize Human-Object Interaction with Radio Frequency Signals
slides.tldr: RF-BASED HUMAN-OBJECT INTERACTION RECOGNITION
slides.highlight: This framework uses mmWave radar and RFID to recognize human-object interactions, offering a privacy-preserving alternative to vision-based sensing for embodied AI and assistive robotics relevant to RwB.

card.one_liner: RF-HOI recognizes human-object interactions using a privacy-preserving fusion of mmWave radar and RFID signals.
card.key_idea: A multimodal framework combining mmWave (for action recognition) and RFID (for target identification) using a transformer-based fusion network and a physics-based RF data simulator.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on 3,615 real-world samples across 78 setups; achieved 96.97% accuracy, outperforming RFID-only and mmWave-only baselines.
card.limitation: Not clearly stated.
